uncited: *   **Hierarchy Tree:** Nodes are organized in levels.
Group nodes represent aggregated bounding volumes of their children.
Leaf nodes represent individual voxel blocks.
*   **Proxy Geometry:** Each node (group or leaf) has an associated proxy geometry (typically an axis-aligned bounding box or simplified mesh) used for rasterization.
**Hierarchy Construction:** Build or traverse the spatial hierarchy.
**Coarse Rasterization:** Rasterize the proxy geometry of the group nodes at a higher level of the hierarchy.
This determines which coarse regions potentially contain visible geometry.
**Ray Traversal Refinement:** For regions identified as potentially visible in the coarse pass, perform ray traversal down the hierarchy tree.
Rays are cast from the camera through the coarse visible regions to intersect with child nodes.
**Leaf Visibility Determination:** Continue traversal until leaf nodes are reached.
A leaf block is marked visible if the ray traversal confirms it is not occluded by previously processed geometry or if it passes the final rasterization test at the leaf level.
**Stream Compaction:** Collect the indices of all visible leaf blocks into a dense list for rendering.
*   **Hierarchy Depth:** The number of levels to rasterize coarsely.
*   **Ray Count:** Number of rays per coarse region.
*   **Time Complexity:** Reduced compared to full leaf rasterization, as only coarse nodes are rasterized initially.
Complexity depends on hierarchy depth and ray traversal cost.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires storage for the hierarchy tree and proxy geometries.
Performance may degrade in highly complex or unstructured scenes where hierarchy balancing is poor.
*   **When to use:** Large-scale volume rendering with high block counts where rasterization is the bottleneck.
*   **When not to use:** Scenes with very few blocks or where ray traversal overhead exceeds rasterization savings.
